title: Indexing and B+ Trees Problem #1
text: In SQL standard relational databases (Query #1), under what condition does the HAVING clause filter rows for this query in Indexing and B+ Trees with threshold 51000?
code_snippet:
SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*) 
FROM Employees 
GROUP BY dept_id 
HAVING AVG(salary) > 51000;
explanation: WHERE filters individual tuples before grouping, whereas HAVING filters aggregated groups after GROUP BY.

options.text: Before individual table rows are grouped
During the initial table scan prior to WHERE evaluation
Only if a nested subquery is explicitly defined
After the GROUP BY aggregation is applied to groups

explanation: In BCNF, for every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y, X must strictly be a superkey.
